cr_data.provenance:
September 16, 1957, sold by Downtown Gallery, New York (stock no. 207), to William H. Lane (b. 1914 - d. 1995), Standard Pyroxoloid Corporation, Leominster, MA [see note 1]; 1990, partial sale and partial gift of William H. and Saundra B. Lane to the MFA. (Accession Date: June 27, 1990) 
 
NOTES: 
[1] Archives of American Art, Downtown Gallery Records, Series 4, Business Records: Sales Slips (2 of 3), 1957: Reel 5628 (Box 73), Frame 1023. 
(Source: MFA Boston, 2025)
remarks_1999: O'Keeffe wrote: "I have a cedar stump painted red against a yellow sky — and when I finished with it discovered that I had two monsters — so I hung it away and forgot it till I had your letter and was looking around — and I have to laugh that I rather like it now" (O'Keeffe to Edith Halpert, 8 August 1954, Archive of American Art). Titled *Red Tree Yellow Sky* by O'Keeffe on Abiquiú Notebooks photograph. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: The twisted, craggy form of a dead tree stands on the left side of the canvas. Its bright red and pink limbs jut into the canvas at several different angles. Beyond the tree, the red silhouette of Pedernal stands below a bright yellow sky.
title: Red Tree – Yellow Sky
